title: Shiksha STEM & Reasoning
description: Scientific constants, physics laws, calculus, biological pathways, chemistry trends, and reasoning fundamentals.

chunks.title: Newton's Laws of Motion & Momentum
chunks.text: Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia): An object remains at rest or in uniform motion along a straight line unless acted upon by an external net force. Second Law: Net force equals the rate of change of linear momentum F = dp/dt = m*a. Third Law: For every action force, there is an equal and opposite reaction force acting on different bodies simultaneously.

chunks.title: Thermodynamics Laws & Carnot Efficiency
chunks.text: Zeroth Law: Defines temperature via thermal equilibrium. First Law (Conservation of Energy): ΔU = Q - W. Second Law: Total entropy of an isolated system never decreases; heat cannot spontaneously flow from cooler to hotter body without work. Carnot engine maximum efficiency: η = 1 - (T_cold / T_hot), where temperatures are in Kelvin.

chunks.title: Photosynthesis Light and Dark Reactions
chunks.text: Photosynthesis equation: 6CO2 + 6H2O + light -> C6H12O6 + 6O2. Light reactions occur in thylakoid membranes, producing ATP and NADPH via photophosphorylation while releasing oxygen from photolysis of water. Dark reactions (Calvin Cycle) occur in the stroma, where RuBisCO enzyme fixes CO2 into 3-PGA, synthesizing glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P).

chunks.title: Fundamental Calculus Derivatives and Integrals
chunks.text: Standard derivative rules: d/dx(x^n) = n*x^(n-1); d/dx(sin x) = cos x; d/dx(cos x) = -sin x; d/dx(e^x) = e^x; d/dx(ln x) = 1/x. Product rule: (u*v)' = u'v + uv'. Chain rule: d/dx[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x))*g'(x). Fundamental Theorem of Calculus connects differentiation and integration: ∫ from a to b of f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a).

chunks.title: Ohm's Law, Resistance & Power in Electrical Circuits
chunks.text: Ohm's Law states current I is proportional to potential difference V: V = I * R. Series resistance: R_total = R1 + R2 + R3. Parallel resistance: 1/R_total = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3. Electrical power dissipated: P = V * I = I^2 * R = V^2 / R. Electrical energy is measured in kilowatt-hours (1 kWh = 3.6 × 10^6 Joules).

chunks.title: Periodic Table Periodic Trends
chunks.text: Electronegativity increases across a period (left to right) and decreases down a group (Fluorine is most electronegative). Atomic radius decreases across a period due to increasing effective nuclear charge, and increases down a group due to addition of electron shells. Ionization Energy increases across a period and decreases down a group.

chunks.title: Optics: Snell's Law and Total Internal Reflection
chunks.text: Snell's Law of refraction: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2), where n is refractive index. Total Internal Reflection (TIR) occurs when light travels from denser to rarer medium (n1 > n2) at an angle of incidence greater than critical angle θc = arcsin(n2/n1). TIR enables optical fiber communications, endoscopes, and diamond brilliance.

chunks.title: Work, Energy and Power Formulas
chunks.text: Work done W = F * d * cos(θ). Kinetic Energy KE = 1/2 * m * v^2. Gravitational Potential Energy PE = m * g * h. Work-Energy Theorem states net work done equals change in kinetic energy: W_net = ΔKE. Law of Conservation of Energy: Total mechanical energy E = KE + PE remains constant in conservative force fields.
